summary:
Malatya province falls entirely under Turkey's national legal framework. No statute, police directive, court decision or incident specific to Malatya appears in the sources consulted, so the position of a trans visitor in the province is the position the central authorities have constructed nationally.

Homosexuality has not been a criminal offence in Turkey since the Ottoman penal code of 1858, and transgender people have been able to change their legal gender since 1988. No comprehensive law prohibits discrimination on the basis of sexual orientation or gender identity. Openly LGBTQ people are barred from serving in the military, and same-sex marriage, civil unions, domestic partnerships and joint adoption are not recognised.

Pride parades have been banned by local authorities since 2015; Istanbul's 2015-2018 parades were banned and dispersed. In June 2025 authorities issued blanket bans against the Istanbul LGBTI and Trans pride marches, police subjected peaceful protesters to unlawful use of force, and over 90 people were arbitrarily detained; prosecutions of 92 people for participating in pride marches continued at year's end.

In December 2025 an İzmir court ordered the dissolution of the Young LGBTI+ Association, ruling it had shared 'obscene' images incompatible with 'society's moral values' that could 'encourage or promote' LGBTI identities. Three draft law packages targeting LGBTI people were made public during 2025 — which would criminalise expression of LGBTI identities and consensual same-sex relations and make legal gender recognition nearly impossible — but they were ultimately not submitted to parliament.

The 12th judicial reform package passed in 2026 dropped provisions discriminating against LGBTQ people and made symbolic same-sex weddings possible, though these carry no legal marital status. In early 2026 Turkish media reported that the government was considering legislation criminalising public advocacy of 'behaviour contrary to biological sex', which was not included in that year's package, and in September 2026 police detained dozens in raids on gay bars and the homes of LGBTQ+ activists under a 'Decade of Family and Population' crackdown.
